purpose: Every accessibility finding G1.13b measures and the product has not answered yet. e2e/a11y.spec.ts makes the four measurements axe cannot make — reflow at a 320 CSS px viewport, target size at 390x844, keyboard traversal at 390x844 and 1280x800, and the equivalent list and text behind every chart — over the same reachable pages the axe sweeps cover, derived from docs/route-register.json so a new page joins all four the day it lands. Two of the four are hard assertions and stay hard: reflow and the text alternatives, for the reasons the notes at the bottom of this file give. The other two compare what they find against the matching group here in both directions: a finding that is not listed fails, and a listed finding that no longer occurs fails too, so a control that reaches 44px or a widget that stops trapping focus has to bring its entry down with it, and neither list can grow without a person writing the entry that admits it.
notAnApproval: Listing a finding records it; it does not bless it. Every entry below is an open WCAG failure measured exactly, not an accepted state — acceptance is a line in docs/acceptance-matrix.md and G1.13b stands at NO there. A 32x32 control is exactly as far from the brief's 44px as it was before it was written down, and a keyboard trap is a Level A failure whether or not this file mentions it. What the ledger buys is that the distance is exact, that it names the decision or the dependency holding it open, and that it can only shrink.
howEntriesAreMatched: The two groups hold fields, not sentences, and e2e/a11y.spec.ts rebuilds the sentence from them through the same two functions the measurements themselves use — undersizedControlFinding and keyboardFinding — so a recorded finding and a present one are the same sentence or they are not the same finding. What the ledger deliberately does not hold is the per-page evidence: which route, which element, the box it measured, the exact order violations. The failing test prints all of it, in full, for every finding that is not recorded, and prints the paste-ready object beside it. Keeping that evidence here would produce a file that churned on every page added while recording nothing a person needs in order to decide anything.
granularity: The target-size group is recorded per component, not per (page, control). One theme toggle at 32x32 is one row here and one finding on every swept route; identical rows repeated once per page would be a worse document than one row that says so — the same decision docs/claims-divergence.json takes when it records 675 unregistered prose blocks as 16 per-file rows, and docs/figures-register.json takes when it records one shape-level invariant instead of 298 identical figure rows. The component is derived from the element's own attributes and nothing else: tag, data-slot, data-variant, data-size, input type, role, and failing all of those the nearest ancestor carrying a data-slot. So it is exactly as precise as the DOM allows and never guesses at a React component, and it is never the accessible name — Save and Delete are two labels on one component, and a per-label ledger would be a per-instance ledger with extra steps. Where the nearest slotted ancestor differs between pages, one logical control lands in two rows rather than one: the grouping errs toward more rows, never toward a row that swallows a finding. Nothing is rounded away by grouping. Every undersized (page, control) pair is still measured and still counted, by UNDERSIZED_CONTROL_OCCURRENCES in e2e/a11y.spec.ts, which is an exact ratchet on the volume these rows collapse — so a component fixed lowers it, a control shrunk or a page added raises it, and the collapse can never hide growth. The keyboard group needs no collapsing: its natural unit is already one (route, viewport, assertion), and there are four.
measuredNotGuessed: Every number in this file came from a sweep, never from a guess. targetSize is EMPTY, measured 2026-09-11 across the 56 swept routes: every undersized control the gate found has been fixed, and UNDERSIZED_CONTROL_OCCURRENCES in e2e/a11y.spec.ts holds 0 as an exact-equality ratchet, so the next control that lands under 44x44 fails the sweep rather than joining a list. It held 990, then 807, then 201 before that change. reflow is EMPTY as of 21 September 2026, its last route fixed rather than recorded - see reflowNote. What is left is one third-party widget: keyboardTraversal carries two rows, both on /genome/[subject]/data/browser at 1280x800 inside igv.js 3.8.5. Their `reached`, `expected` and `violations` fields are evidence rather than the compared key: they move between runs on unchanged code, because the count of certainly-tabbable elements depends on what the swept account holds.

keyboardTraversal.why: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap, Level A. Tab past the last control does not hand focus out of the page: it returns to a stop the traversal has already visited. The last stop is the container itself - src/components/browse/genome-browser.tsx renders a role=region div named by IGV_CONTROL_LABELS.region ('Interactive genome browser') and hands its DOM to igv; it is a horizontal scroller (overflow-x-auto), which is there so the browser reflows at the 320px support floor instead of widening the document to 485px. Everything that holds focus after it belongs to igv. The test is careful about what it can and cannot tell apart here: focus leaving the document and a headless wrap to the first stop both count as leaving, and only a return to something that is not the first stop counts as a trap. This is the second kind. The Level A criterion is now met, and this entry is the tab-order defect that remains, not a conformance failure. SC 2.1.2 does not require Tab to be the key. It requires that focus can be moved away using only the keyboard, and that where the key is not an unmodified arrow or Tab, the reader is told which key it is. Both are shipped: the container binds Escape in the capture phase on our own element - never by reaching into igv's DOM - and moves focus to the next thing a Tab would have reached after the region, so the traversal continues forwards rather than restarting; and BROWSER_KEYBOARD_ESCAPE is rendered above the region and referenced by it through aria-describedby, so a reader arriving by Tab is told on entry rather than only if they happened to look. What stays recorded here is the thing that is still wrong: Tab alone should have been enough, and inside this widget it is not.
keyboardTraversal.closing: Upstream, a fork, or a replacement, as with the row above - the tab order inside the widget is igv.js 3.8.5's. The interim this entry used to ask for is built rather than described, and the sweep now enforces it rather than trusting it: a traversal that ends trapped is additionally required to escape, and that check is a plain failure, not a ledger entry, because an unescapable trap has no honest interim. It reads the key from the component's own accessible description rather than assuming Escape, so a page that advertises a different key is checked against what it advertises and a page that advertises nothing fails on that alone; it then requires focus to land outside the region and forwards of it, because moving focus backwards would satisfy the letter and strand the reader before the widget they just left. A floor asserts the check ran at least once, so it cannot quietly stop running and leave this entry as the only thing saying the trap exists.
keyboardTraversal.blocker: third party - the focus order inside the widget is igv.js 3.8.5's, and the container is the last element of ours that the traversal reaches. Not a blocker on SC 2.1.2, which the shipped escape meets.

keyboardTraversal.why: Three order violations on the variant browser at desktop width. One of the three is the trap's own entry — a traversal that ends trapped records 'focus returned to ...' before it stops — so two are order breaks in their own right. The markup they walk is not ours: everything inside the container is built by igv.js 3.8.5 (package.json), which renders part of its navbar into a shadow root, and src/components/browse/genome-browser.tsx can only post-process what igv builds, attaching accessible names and button roles after createBrowser resolves, best effort inside try/catch so an igv upgrade that renames a class degrades rather than crashes. DOM order inside a widget we do not author is not something a post-processing pass can rewrite without taking ownership of the widget's layout.
keyboardTraversal.closing: A fix upstream in igv.js, a fork, or replacing the widget. A fourth option that would close it here — rebuilding the navbar ourselves from igv's API and hiding its own — is a larger change than it sounds, because the navbar igv renders into a shadow root is the same DOM its zoom and locus behaviour is bound to.
keyboardTraversal.blocker: third party — igv.js 3.8.5 builds and owns this subtree, shadow root included

reflowNote: Reflow at 320 CSS px is a hard assertion in e2e/a11y.spec.ts for every route, and the group above is now EMPTY. It failed on 33 routes when the sweep was first written; 32 were fixed rather than recorded - the marketing header, which alone accounted for 31 because it laid the wordmark, the theme toggle and two auth controls in a row needing 344px against a 320px viewport, and the /files action row at 370px. Both wrap now. The 33rd, /genome/[subject]/data/browser, was carried here by exact measured width (485px, then 446px once its igv container became a horizontal scroller) while its cause stayed unidentified. It is fixed, 21 September 2026, and the cause was named by the sweep itself rather than by reading: the genotype figure's `sr-only` label is `position: absolute` under Tailwind (position absolute, width 1px, margin -1px, clip-path inset(50%)), so it was NOT clipped by the `overflow-x-auto` claim block around the 593px results table, because that section was `position: static` and a static ancestor's overflow does not clip an absolutely positioned descendant. The 1px label sat at its static position inside the wide table, past the viewport edge, and carried the document to 446px. The scrolling claim block is now `relative`, which makes it the containing block for its own out-of-flow descendants and therefore clips them. Only the scrolling variant takes it; an ordinary claim block is not a clipper and must not silently become one. An empty group is the strict state: any route that scrolls sideways at 320 CSS px now fails outright rather than joining a list, and nothing may be added here without a person writing the entry that admits it.
textAlternativesNote: Not a group either, and for the better reason: it passes. The ancestry map and every chart the sweep finds carry an equivalent list and text — inside the figure, on the far end of its own aria-describedby, or beside it in the container that holds them both — reachable without a pointer, in zero activations. It stays a hard assertion so that stays true, and it is the one of the four measurements that needs nothing from this file.
keyboardTraversalNote: Two kinds of finding were recorded here and one of them was never real. The stop shortfalls - eight on the report library at both widths, one on /copilot/[scope] - were the sweep counting controls that sit inside a closed `details`. Chromium still gives those descendants client rects, so the counter said they were rendered and expected Tab to reach them; Tab is right not to, because the summary that opens the disclosure is itself a tab stop and is counted and reached. The report library's eight are its category jump links, behind the collapsed filter strip that the first-viewport interactive budget requires. Naming the elements rather than counting them is what showed this: 'eight stops missing' reads like eight controls a keyboard cannot reach, and 'never reached: a "Everyday traits", a "Cancer", ...' reads like a disclosure. The counter excludes closed-disclosure descendants now, and no stop shortfall survives it. What remains below is the genome browser, where the findings are real.
